correctness.rationale: For a 3-coprime argument the quotient sum is congruent to n(c_+−c_−), since every exact prime power is its own inverse modulo 3. Taking the imaginary part after multiplying the cubic character phase by χ(n) encodes the signed residue indicator and gives a multiplicative bounded coefficient sequence. For n=3^a u with a≥1 the residue is u, so the total discrepancy from this case is O(log X). The prime-power coefficients give the two stated local factors and the prime coefficient z−χ(p)/2 away from 3. First-order cancellation gives H by normally convergent O(p^(−2σ)) corrections near 1. At 1, every E_p for p≥5 is within 1/(p−1) of 1 and E_2 is explicitly nonzero; the normalization factors are nonzero. For the analytic estimate use Granville–Koukoulopoulos Theorem 1 with |f|≤τ_1 and prime-sum exponent z, taking A=3 by the fixed-modulus prime number theorem. It yields the leading coefficient lim_(s→1)(s−1)^z F(s) divided by Γ(z), with all lower terms and the remainder O(X/log²X). This explicitly supplies the error hypothesis missing from the original abbreviated appeal to local holomorphy. The unbounded log-log phase attains both extrema on sequences; the normalized error vanishes. The stated densities can also be checked independently: the unweighted cubic phase on 3-coprime n has prime mean (ω+ω²)/2=−1/2, hence mean zero by the same theorem. Its real part determines the zero-residue indicator on coprimes, leaving total density 7/9 for the nonzero classes after adding the multiples of 3; D=o(X) splits it equally. This does not verify the historical all-modulus attribution. The supplied finite checker was inspected, not executed.
